constructedEnvironment.CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION: Runtime support code for the AWS SDK. This isn't intended to be used directly.
Types and traits for working with bytes

A macro to ergonomically define an item depending on a large number of #[cfg]
parameters. Structured like an if-else chain, the first matching branch is the
item that gets emitted.

Conditional move CPU intrinsics which are guaranteed on major platforms (ARM32/ARM64, x86/x86_64,
RISC-V) to execute in constant-time and not be rewritten as branches by the compiler. Provides
wrappers for the CMOV family of instructions on x86/x86_64 and CSEL on AArch64, along with a
portable "best-effort" pure Rust fallback implementation.

Const-friendly implementation of the ISO/IEC Object Identifier (OID) standard
as defined in ITU X.660, with support for BER/DER encoding/decoding as well as
heapless no_std (i.e. embedded) support
Catalog of CRC algorithms (generated from http://reveng.sourceforge.net/crc-catalogue) expressed as simple Rust structs.
Ranged integers
The enum `Either` with variants `Left` and `Right` is a general purpose sum type with two cases.
A simple and fast random number generator
Fowler–Noll–Vo hash function
A fast, non-cryptographic, minimally DoS-resistant hashing algorithm.
The core traits and types in for the `futures` library.
Tools for working with tasks.
Encoding and decoding data into/from hexadecimal representation.
Fast integer primitive to string conversion
A key-value Map implementation based on a flat, sorted Vec.

`num_conv` is a crate to convert between integer types without using `as` casts. This provides
better certainty when refactoring, makes the exact behavior of code more explicit, and allows using
turbofish syntax.
Single assignment cells and lazy values.
Out reference
Percent encoding and decoding
A lightweight version of pin-project written with declarative macros.
Utilities for pinning

`powerfmt` is a library that provides utilities for formatting values. This crate makes it
    significantly easier to support filling to a minimum width with alignment, avoid heap
    allocation, and avoid repetitive calculations.
Fast floating point to string conversion
'Small vector' optimization: store up to a small number of items on the stack

constructedEnvironment.CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION: Spin-based synchronization primitives
An unsafe marker trait for types like Box and Rc that dereference to a stable address even when moved, and hence can be used with libraries such as owning_ref and rental.
This crate is an implementation detail and should not be relied upon directly.

Typenum is a Rust library for type-level numbers evaluated at
    compile time. It currently supports bits, unsigned integers, and signed
    integers. It also provides a type-level array of type-level numbers, but its
    implementation is incomplete.
Safe, fast, zero-panic, zero-crashing, zero-allocation parsing of untrusted inputs in Rust.
Iterator by char over potentially-invalid UTF-8 in &[u8]
A library to generate and parse UUIDs.
SIMD utilities
A more efficient alternative to fmt::Display

Securely clear secrets from memory with a simple trait built on
stable Rust primitives which guarantee memory is zeroed using an
operation will not be 'optimized away' by the compiler.
Uses a portable pure Rust implementation that works everywhere,
even WASM!
SIMD-accelerated base64 encoding and decoding
Additional utilities for working with the bytes crate
Rust implementation of CRC with support of various standards

Constant-time utility library with selection and equality testing support targeting cryptographic
applications. Supports `const fn` where appropriate. Built on the `cmov` crate which provides
architecture-specific predication intrinsics. Heavily inspired by the `subtle` crate.
Parser and serializer for the application/x-www-form-urlencoded syntax, as used by HTML forms.
Common utilities and extension traits for the futures-rs library.
A Rust port of Google's SwissTable hash map
A set of types for representing HTTP requests and responses.
A set of types for representing HTTP requests and responses.

Hybrid typenum-based and const generic array types designed to provide the
flexibility of typenum-based expressions while also allowing interoperability
and a transition path to const generics
Date and time library. Fully interoperable with the standard library. Mostly compatible with #![no_std].

An event-driven, non-blocking I/O platform for writing asynchronous I/O
backed applications.
Core primitives for application-level tracing.
Async runtime agnostic abstractions for smithy-rs.
Buffer types for block processing of data
Common traits used by cryptographic algorithms
Trait representing an asynchronous, streaming, HTTP request or response body.
Trait representing an asynchronous, streaming, HTTP request or response body.
A LRU cache implementation
Traits for cryptographic hash functions and message authentication codes
Combinators and adapters for HTTP request or response bodies.
Generic implementation of Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC)
MD5 hash function

Provides types and useful methods for working with IPv4 and IPv6 network addresses, commonly called IP prefixes. The new `IpNet`, `Ipv4Net`, and `Ipv6Net` types build on the existing `IpAddr`, `Ipv4Addr`, and `Ipv6Addr` types already provided in Rust's standard library and align to their design to stay consistent. The module also provides useful traits that extend `Ipv4Addr` and `Ipv6Addr` with methods for `Add`, `Sub`, `BitAnd`, and `BitOr` operations. The module only uses stable feature so it is guaranteed to compile using the stable toolchain.

Provides types and useful methods for working with IPv4 and IPv6 network addresses, commonly called IP prefixes. The new `IpNet`, `Ipv4Net`, and `Ipv6Net` types build on the existing `IpAddr`, `Ipv4Addr`, and `Ipv6Addr` types already provided in Rust's standard library and align to their design to stay consistent. The module also provides useful traits that extend `Ipv4Addr` and `Ipv6Addr` with methods for `Add`, `Sub`, `BitAnd`, and `BitOr` operations. The module only uses stable feature so it is guaranteed to compile using the stable toolchain.
